2	title: cacheComponents
3	description: Learn how to enable the cacheComponents flag in Next.js.
4	related:
5	  links:
6	    - app/getting-started/caching
7	    - app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components
8	    - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache
9	    - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote
10	---
11	
12	Cache Components enables component and function-level caching using the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive. Data fetching is dynamic by default, and you choose what to cache at the page, component, or function level. Next.js prerenders a static HTML shell that is served immediately while dynamic content streams in when ready, letting you mix static and dynamic content within a single route.
13	
14	## Usage
15	
16	To enable the `cacheComponents` flag, set it to `true` in your `next.config.ts` file:
17	
18	```ts filename="next.config.ts"
19	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
20	
21	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
22	  cacheComponents: true,
23	}
24	
25	export default nextConfig
26	```
27	
28	> **Good to know**: Cache Components requires the Node.js runtime. Migrate any routes that set the deprecated `runtime = 'edge'` export, and note that other server-side JavaScript runtimes are not guaranteed to work. See [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components#runtime--edge).
29	
30	When `cacheComponents` is enabled, you can use the following cache functions and configurations:
31	
32	- The [`use cache` directive](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache)
33	- The [`cacheLife` function](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife) with `use cache`
34	- The [`cacheTag` function](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag)
35	
36	> **Good to know**: If you used `experimental.useCache` or `experimental.dynamicIO`, migrate using the [Version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#experimentaldynamicio-and-experimentalusecache). To migrate route segment configs and other caching patterns, see [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components).
37	
38	Additionally, `cacheComponents` implements **[Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prerendering-ppr)** as the default behavior in the App Router. This means the `experimental.ppr` configuration flag and the `experimental_ppr` route segment configuration are no longer necessary and have been removed.
39	
40	Read [Prerendering](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#prerendering) for how the static shell and streaming fit together.
41	
42	> **Good to know**: If you used experimental PPR in Next.js 15, refer to the [Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#partial-prerendering-ppr) section of the Version 16 upgrade guide when migrating.
43	
44	## Navigation with Activity
45	
46	When `cacheComponents` is enabled, Next.js uses React's [`<Activity>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity) component to preserve component state during client-side navigation.
47	
48	Rather than unmounting the previous route when you navigate away, Next.js sets the Activity mode to [`"hidden"`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity#activity). This means:
49	
50	- Component state is preserved when navigating between routes
51	- When you navigate back, the previous route reappears with its state intact
52	- Effects are cleaned up when a route is hidden, and recreated when it becomes visible again
53	
54	This behavior improves the navigation experience by maintaining UI state (form inputs, or expanded sections) when users navigate back and forth between routes.
55	
56	> **Good to know**: Next.js uses heuristics to keep a few recently visited routes `"hidden"`, while older routes are removed from the DOM to prevent excessive growth.
57	
58	Some UI patterns behave differently when components stay mounted instead of unmounting. See the [Preserving UI state guide](/docs/app/guides/preserving-ui-state) for handling common patterns like dropdowns, dialogs, and testing.
59	
60	## Version History
61	
62	| Version | Change                                                                                                                            |
63	| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
64	| 16.0.0  | `cacheComponents` introduced. This flag controls the `ppr`, `useCache`, and `dynamicIO` flags as a single, unified configuration. |
65

With Cache Components enabled, Next.js validates in development whether navigating into each route renders instantly, and surfaces the code that would block it as an error or insight. 21 22 ## Use the adoption skill (recommended) 23 24 The [`next-cache-components-adoption`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/skills/next-cache-components-adoption) skill drives this migration with a coding agent, one feature at a time, checking in at every feature boundary. It supports two modes: 25 26 - **Incremental.** Opens a single mechanical PR that opts every route out of validation, then ships each feature as a follow-up PR. This automates the [Adopting incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) flow below. 27 - **Direct.** Adopts every route in place on one branch. 28 29 Install the skill: 30 31 ```bash filename="Terminal" 32 npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-cache-components-adoption 33 ``` 34 35 Then give the agent this prompt: 36 37 ```prompt 38 Adopt Cache Components in this project using the next-cache-components-adoption skill. 39 ``` 40 41 ## Or migrate by hand 42 43 Migrating an existing app by hand follows a few steps, in order: 44 45 1. [Enable Cache Components](#enable-cache-components) in `next.config.ts`. 46 2. Decide your approach: convert every route now, or [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) by [opting routes out of validation](#opting-out-of-validation) first and converting one at a time. 47 3. [Follow the validation errors and insights](#following-validation) it surfaces, replacing each route segment config with its Cache Components equivalent and caching uncached data with [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) or wrapping runtime data in [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense). The per-key sections below cover each config and API. 48 49 Your existing `fetch` and `unstable_cache` caching keeps working as a separate layer, so let the insights and errors guide what to change. 50 51 Some surfaces have their own steps: 52 53 - For routes with dynamic params, follow the [`generateStaticParams`](#generatestaticparams-and-dynamicparams) guidance. 54 - For metadata, follow the [`generateMetadata` and `generateViewport`](#generatemetadata-and-generateviewport) guidance. 55 56 The sections below cover each config and API and what to do with it under Cache Components. 57 58 ## Enable Cache Components 59 60 Cache Components requires Next.js 16. If you're on Next.js 15 or earlier, upgrade first by following the [version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16). Coming from an older version, work through the [upgrade guides](/docs/app/guides/upgrading) to reach 16 before continuing. 61 62 Then enable the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) flag in `next.config.ts`: 63 64 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 65 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 66 67 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 68 cacheComponents: true, 69 } 70 71 export default nextConfig 72 ``` 73 74 > **Good to know:** If you were using `experimental.dynamicIO` or `experimental.useCache`, `cacheComponents` replaces them. See the [version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#experimentaldynamicio-and-experimentalusecache). 75 76 After enabling the flag, route segments that still export `dynamic`, `revalidate`, or `fetchCache` will error. Start by replacing those configs. The sections below explain what to do for each one. 77 78 ## Opting out of validation 79 80 A validation insight or error tells you a route won't render instantly. Resolve it by following the recommendation: cache the data with [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) or wrap it in [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense). If you're not ready to address it yet, set the [`instant`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) config to `false` on the segment that raised it (a layout, page, or parallel slot), then come back to it later. 81 82 ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx" 83 export const instant = false 84 ``` 85 86 > **Good to know**: `instant = false` marks a segment as _allowed to block_. It does not force the route to be dynamic, so a genuinely prerenderable route still ships a static shell. It also does not clear synchronous IO build errors: calls like `new Date()`, `Math.random()`, and `crypto.randomUUID()` still fail the prerender. See [Adopting incrementally](#adopting-incrementally). 87 88 ## Adopting incrementally 89 90 You don't have to migrate every route at once. `instant = false` lets you get the whole app building and running first, then convert routes one at a time: 91 92 1. **Enable the flag and migrate each route segment config.** Follow the relevant sections below for [`dynamic = "force-dynamic"`](#dynamic--force-dynamic), [`dynamic = "force-static"`](#dynamic--force-static), [`revalidate`](#revalidate), and [`fetchCache`](#fetchcache). For routes with dynamic params, also follow the [`generateStaticParams`](#generatestaticparams-and-dynamicparams) guidance. Routes that still render instantly need no further work. 93 2. **Opt out the routes that aren't ready.** Where an insight or error appears, set `instant = false` on the segment that raised it. To do this in one pass across the whole app, run the [`cache-components-instant-false`](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#cache-components-instant-false) codemod, which adds the opt-out to every `page`, `layout`, and `default` that doesn't already declare `instant`: 94 95 ```bash filename="Terminal" 96 npx @next/codemod@canary cache-components-instant-false ./app 97 ``` 98 99 > **Good to know**: Pass `./src/app` in a `src/` project. {product.name}
301 } 302 ``` 303 304 ### Custom profiles for specific needs 305 306 Define custom profiles when preset options don't match your requirements: 307 308 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 309 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 310 311 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 312 cacheComponents: true, 313 cacheLife: { 314 editorial: { 315 stale: 600, // 10 minutes 316 revalidate: 3600, // 1 hour 317 expire: An equally valid approach is to define your own [custom profile](#custom-cache-profiles) rather than overloading a built-in name. 154 155 Redefining `default` also changes the lifetime applied when a `use cache` scope calls no `cacheLife`. The example below sets `default` to a one hour revalidate: 156 157 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 158 const nextConfig = { 159 cacheComponents: true, 160 cacheLife: { 161 // Redefine the 'default' profile 162 default: { 163 stale: 300, // 5 minutes 164 revalidate: 3600, // 1 hour 165 expire: 86400, // 1 day 166 }, 167 }, 168 } 169 170 export default nextConfig 171 ``` 172 173 > **Good to know:** The `cacheLife` function's type signature is generated from `next.config.ts` during `next dev`, `next build`, or [`next typegen`](/docs/app/api-reference/cli/next#next-typegen-options), so an overridden profile's editor autocomplete and JSDoc hint reflect the values you set, not the presets. 174 175 ### Custom cache profiles 176 177 Define reusable cache profiles with your own names in `next.config.ts`: 178 179 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 180 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 181 182 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 183 cacheComponents: true, 184 cacheLife: { 185 biweekly: { 186 stale: 60 * 60 * 24 * 14, // 14 days 187 revalidate: 60 * 60 * 24, // 1 day 188 expire: 60 * 60 * 24 * 14, // 14 days 189 }, 190 }, 191 } 192 193 export default nextConfig 194 ``` 195 196 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 197 const nextConfig = { 198 cacheComponents: true, 199 cacheLife: { 200 biweekly: { 201 stale: 60 * 60 * 24 * 14, // 14 days 202 revalidate: 60 * 60 * 24, // 1 day 203 expire: 60 * 60 * 24 * 14, // 14 days 204 }, 205 }, 206 } 207 208 module.exports = nextConfig 209 ``` 210 211 The example above caches for 14 days, checks for updates daily, and expires the cache after 14 days. You can then reference this profile throughout your application by its name: 212 213 > **Good to know**: Any omitted properties in a custom profile inherit from the `default` profile. Page
222 } 223 ``` 224 225 ### Inline cache profiles 226 227 For one-off cases, pass a profile object directly to `cacheLife`: 228 229 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" 230 'use cache' 231 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 232 233 export default async function Page() { 234 cacheLife({ 235 stale: 3600, 236 revalidate: 900, 237 expire: 86400, 238 }) 239 240 return
Page
241 } 242 ``` 243 244 Inline profiles apply only to the specific function or component. For reusable configurations, define custom profiles in `next.config.ts`. 245 246 Using `cacheLife({})` with an empty object applies the `default` profile values. 247 248 ### Client cache behavior 249 250 The `stale` property controls the [Client Cache](/docs/app/glossary#client-cache), not the `Cache-Control` header: 251 252 - The server sends the stale time via the `x-nextjs-stale-time` response header 253 - The client router uses this value to determine when to revalidate 254 - **Minimum of 30 seconds is enforced** to ensure prefetched links remain usable 255 256 This 30-second minimum prevents prefetched data from expiring before users can click on links. It only applies to time-based expiration. 257 258 When you call revalidation functions from a Server Action ([`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag), [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath), [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag), or [`refresh`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/refresh)), the entire client cache is immediately cleared, bypassing the stale time. 259 260 > **Good to know**: The `stale` property in `cacheLife` differs from [`staleTimes`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/staleTimes). While `staleTimes` is a global setting affecting all routes, `cacheLife` allows per-function or per-route configuration. Updating `staleTimes.static` also updates the `stale` value of the `default` cache profile. 261 262 ### Prerendering behavior 263 264 A short cache lifetime changes where the cached content can be delivered from: 265 266 - **`revalidate` of `0`, or `expire` under 5 minutes**: excluded from prerenders, becoming a "dynamic hole" resolved at request time. 267 - **`stale` under 30 seconds**: excluded from prerenders, because a prefetch would expire before the user could click. 268 - **`stale` of at least 30 seconds but under 5 minutes**: included in prerenders, but excluded from the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). 269 270 Of the presets, only `seconds` falls under any of these thresholds: its `expire` of 1 minute excludes it from prerenders. 271 272 This behavior allows you to mix static and dynamic content within the same page. Static parts are prerendered, while short-lived caches create boundaries where data is fetched at request time rather than build time. Use a `` boundary around dynamic caches to provide a fallback while content loads. 273 274 ## Examples 275 276 ### Using preset profiles 277 278 The simplest way to configure caching is using preset profiles. {post.content}
289 } 290 ``` 291 292 ```tsx filename="app/products/[id]/page.tsx" 293 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 294 295 export default async function ProductPage() { 296 'use cache' 297 cacheLife('hours') // Product data updated multiple times per day 298 299 const product = await fetchProduct() 300 return
{product.name}
301 } 302 ``` 303 304 ### Custom profiles for specific needs 305 306 Define custom profiles when preset options don't match your requirements: 307 308 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 309 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 310 311 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 312 cacheComponents: true, 313 cacheLife: { 314 editorial: { 315 stale: 600, // 10 minutes 316 revalidate: 3600, // 1 hour 317 expire: 86400, // 1 day 318 }, 319 marketing: { 320 stale: 300, // 5 minutes 321 revalidate: 1800, // 30 minutes 322 expire: 43200, // 12 hours 323 }, 324 }, 325 } 326 327 export default nextConfig 328 ``` caching behavior: 345 346 ```tsx filename="app/api/limited-offer/route.ts" 347 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 348 import { getDb } from '@lib/db' 349 350 async function getLimitedOffer() { 351 'use cache' 352 353 cacheLife({ 354 stale: 60, // 1 minute 355 revalidate: 300, // 5 minutes 356 expire: 3600, // 1 hour 357 }) 358 359 const offer = await getDb().offer.findFirst({ 360 where: { type: 'limited' }, 361 orderBy: { created_at: 'desc' }, 362 }) 363 364 return offer 365 } 366 367 export async function GET() { 368 const offer = await getLimitedOffer() 369 370 return Response.json(offer) 371 } 372 ``` 373 374 ### Caching individual functions 375 376 Apply caching to utility functions for granular control: 377 378 ```tsx filename="lib/api.ts" 379 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 380 381 export async function getSettings() { 382 'use cache' 383 cacheLife('max') // Settings rarely change 384 385 return await fetchSettings() 386 } 387 ``` 388 389 ```tsx filename="lib/stats.ts" } 398 ``` 399 400 ### Nested caching behavior 401 402 When you nest `use cache` directives (a cached function or component using another cached function or component), the outer cache's behavior depends on whether it has an explicit `cacheLife`. 403 404 #### With explicit outer cacheLife 405 406 The outer cache uses its own lifetime, regardless of inner cache lifetimes. Inner caches with shorter lifetimes can reduce the outer cache's `default` lifetime. Inner caches with longer lifetimes cannot extend it beyond the default. 428 429 ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" 430 import { Widget } from './widget' 431 432 export default async function Dashboard() { 433 'use cache' 434 // No cacheLife call - uses default (15 min) 435 // If Widget has 5 min → Dashboard becomes 5 min 436 // If Widget has 1 hour → Dashboard stays 15 min 437 438 return ( 439

See [Runtime caching considerations](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#runtime-caching-considerations) for more details. 538 539 ### Conditional cache lifetimes 540 541 You can call `cacheLife` conditionally in different code paths to set different cache durations based on your application logic: 542 543 ```tsx filename="lib/posts.ts" highlight={14,19} 544 import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache' 545 546 async function getPostContent(slug: string) { 547 'use cache' 548 549 const post = await fetchPost(slug) 550 551 // Tag the cache entry for targeted revalidation 552 cacheTag(`post-${slug}`) 553 554 if (!post) { 555 // Content may not be published yet or could be in draft 556 // Cache briefly to reduce database load 557 cacheLife('minutes') 558 return null 559 } 560 561 // Published content can be cached longer 562 cacheLife('days') 563 564 // Return only the necessary data to keep cache size minimal 565 return post.data 566 } 567 ``` 568 569 This pattern is useful when different outcomes need different cache durations, for example, when an item is missing but is likely to be available later. 570 571 #### Using dynamic cache lifetimes from data 572 573 If you want to calculate cache lifetime at runtime, for example by reading it from the fetched data, use an [inline cache profile](#inline-cache-profiles) object: 574 575 ```tsx filename="lib/posts.ts" highlight={15,16,17,18} 576 import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache' 577 578 async function getPostContent(slug: string) { 579 'use cache' 580 581 const post = await fetchPost(slug) 582 cacheTag(`post-${slug}`) 583 584 if (!post) { 585 cacheLife('minutes') 586 return null 587 } 588 589 // Use cache timing from CMS data directly as an object 590 cacheLife({ 591 // Ensure post.revalidateSeconds is a number in seconds 592 // stale and expire inherit from 'default' profile 593 revalidate: post.revalidateSeconds ?? 3600, 594 }) 595 596 return post.data 597 } 598 ``` 599

1 --- 2 title: use cache 3 description: Learn how to use the "use cache" directive to cache data in your Next.js application. 4 related: 5 title: Related 6 description: View related API references. 7 links: 8 - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private 9 - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents 10 - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife 11 - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheHandlers 12 - app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag 13 - app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife 14 - app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag 15 --- 16 17 The `use cache` directive allows you to mark a route, React component, or a function as cacheable. It can be used at the top of a file to indicate that all exports in the file should be cached, or inline at the top of a function or component to cache the return value. Functions and components that use `use cache` must be async. 18 19 > **Good to know:** 20 > 21 > - To use cookies or headers, read them outside cached scopes and pass values as arguments. This is the preferred pattern. 22 > - If the in-memory cache isn't sufficient for runtime data, [`'use cache: remote'`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote) allows platforms to provide a dedicated cache handler, though it requires a network roundtrip to check the cache and typically incurs platform fees. 23 > - For compliance requirements or when you can't refactor to pass runtime data as arguments to a `use cache` scope, see [`'use cache: private'`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private). 24 25 ## Usage 26 27 `use cache` is a Cache Components feature. To enable it, add the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) option to your `next.config.ts` file: 28 29 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 30 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 31 32 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 33 cacheComponents: true, 34 } 35 36 export default nextConfig 37 ``` 38 39 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 40 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 41 const nextConfig = { 42 cacheComponents: true, 43 } 44 45 module.exports = nextConfig 46 ``` 47 48 Then, add `use cache` at the function, component, or file level. Cached functions and components must be async: 49 50 ```tsx 51 // Function level 52 export async function getData() { 53 'use cache' 54 const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 55 const data = await res.json() 56 return data 57 } 58 59 // Component level 60 export async function MyComponent() { 61 'use cache' 62 return <> 63 } 64 ``` 65 66 When used at file level, every exported function becomes a cached function and must also be async: 67 68 ```tsx 69 // File level 70 'use cache' 71 72 export default async function Page() { 73 // ... 74 } 75 ``` 76 77 ## How `use cache` works 78 79 ### Cache keys 80 81 A cache entry's key is generated using a serialized version of its inputs, which includes: 82 83 1. **Build ID** - Unique per build, changing this invalidates all cache entries. If [`deploymentId`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/deploymentId) is configured, it overrides the build ID for cache key purposes. 84 2. **Function ID** - A secure hash of the function's location and signature in the codebase 85 3. **Serializable arguments** - Props (for components) or function arguments 86 4. **HMR refresh hash** (development only) - Invalidates cache on hot module replacement 87 88 When a cached function references variables from outer scopes, those variables are automatically captured and bound as arguments, making them part of the cache key. 89 90 ```tsx filename="lib/data.ts" 91 async function Component({ userId }: { userId: string }) { 92 const getData = async (filter: string) => { 93 'use cache' 94 // Cache key includes both userId (from closure) and filter (argument) 95 const res = await fetch( 96 `https://api.example.com/users/${userId}/data?filter=${filter}` 97 ) 98 return res.json() 99 } 100 101 return getData('active') 102 } 103 ``` 104 105 In the snippet above, `userId` is captured from the outer scope and `filter` is passed as an argument, so both become part of the `getData` function's cache key. This means different user and filter combinations will have separate cache entries. 106 107 > **Good to know:** When a cached function reads [root parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-root-params), only the ones it actually reads become part of its cache key. 108 109 ### Cache output 110 111 A cached function produces the same output for the same inputs. The first call with a given set of inputs runs the function body and stores its output. Every later call with the same inputs reuses that output, within a render pass and across requests, for as long as the entry lasts. 112 113 Outputs are stored by a [cache handler](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheHandlers), [in memory](#runtime-caching-considerations) by default, and last until they [revalidate](#revalidation). 114 115 ```tsx filename="lib/orders.ts" 116 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 117 118 export async function getOrderSummary(accountId: string) { 119 'use cache' 120 cacheLife('hours') 121 122 const orders = await getOrders(accountId) 123 const totals = await getOrderTotals(accountId) 124 125 return { orders, totals } 126 } 127 128 export async function getOrders(accountId: string) { 129 'use cache' 130 cacheLife('hours') 131 132 return db.orders.findMany({ where: { accountId } }) 133 } 134 135 export async function getOrderTotals(accountId: string) { 136 return db.orders.aggregate({ where: { accountId }, _sum: { amount: true } }) 137 } 138 ``` 139 140 In the example above, each `accountId` has its own entry for `getOrderSummary`, holding the serialized `{ orders, totals }` object it returns. Calls to `getOrders` have their own entries, keyed by the same `accountId`. If an earlier call, through the summary or directly, already filled one, `db.orders.findMany` doesn't run and those orders become part of the summary's output. See [nested caching behavior](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#nested-caching-behavior) for how an inner lifetime affects the entry around it. 141 142 Note that `getOrderTotals` is not cached. It is exported so other parts of the application can read fresh totals in an uncached scope. Inside `getOrderSummary`, though, the totals query only runs when that function runs following the `'hours'` lifetime set there. 143 144 With [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), prerendering fills the entry and keeps rendering, so this output contributes to the route's [static shell](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#prerendering) and can contribute to its [prefetch](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#prefetching). A cache life too short to store safely leaves a hole that resolves at request time instead. See [prerendering behavior](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#prerendering-behavior) for the thresholds. 145 146 ## Serialization 147 148 Arguments to cached functions and their return values must be serializable. 149 150 For a complete reference, see: 151 152 - [Serializable arguments](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-server#serializable-parameters-and-return-values) - Uses **React Server Components** serialization 153 - [Serializable return types](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client#serializable-types) - Uses **React Client Components** serialization 154 155 > **Good to know:** Arguments and return values use different serialization systems. Server Component serialization (for arguments) is more restrictive than Client Component serialization (for return values). This means you can return JSX elements but cannot accept them as arguments unless using pass-through patterns. 156 157 ### Supported types 158 159 **Arguments:** 160 161 - Primitives: `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `null`, `undefined` 162 - Plain objects: `{ key: value }` 163 - Arrays: `[1, 2, 3]` 164 - Dates, Maps, Sets, TypedArrays, ArrayBuffers 165 - React elements (as pass-through only) 166 167 **Return values:** 168 169 - Same as arguments, plus JSX elements 170 171 ### Unsupported types 172 173 - Class instances 174 - Functions (except as pass-through) 175 - Symbols, WeakMaps, WeakSets 176 - URL instances 177 178 ```tsx filename="app/components/user-card.tsx" 179 // Valid - primitives and plain objects 180 async function UserCard({ 181 id, 182 config, 183 }: { 184 id: string 185 config: { theme: string } 186 }) { 187 'use cache' 188 return
{id}
189 } 190 191 // Invalid - class instance 192 async function UserProfile({ user }: { user: UserClass }) { 193 'use cache' 194 // Error: Cannot serialize class instance 195 return
{user.name}
196 } 197 ``` 198 199 ### Pass-through (non-serializable arguments) 200 201 You can accept non-serializable values **as long as you don't introspect them**. This enables composition patterns with `children` and Server Actions: 202 203 ```tsx filename="app/components/cached-wrapper.tsx" 204 async function CachedWrapper({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) { 205 'use cache' 206 // Don't read or modify children - just pass it through 207 return ( 208
209
Cached Header
210 {children} 211
212 ) 213 } 214 215 // Usage: children can be dynamic 216 export default function Page() { 217 return ( 218 219 {/* Not cached, passed through */} 220 221 ) 222 } 223 ``` 224 225 You can also pass Server Actions through cached components: 226 227 ```tsx filename="app/components/cached-form.tsx" 228 async function CachedForm({ action }: { action: () => Promise }) { 229 'use cache' 230 // Don't call action here - just pass it through 231 return
{/* ... */}
232 } 233 ``` 234 235 ## Constraints 236 237 Cached functions execute in an isolated environment. The following constraints ensure cache behavior remains predictable and secure. 238 239 ### Request-time APIs 240 241 Cached functions and components **cannot** access runtime APIs like `cookies()`, `headers()`, or `searchParams`, and the restriction follows the call stack: a helper the cached function calls that reads one of these fails the same way, with the [`next-request-in-use-cache`](/docs/messages/next-request-in-use-cache) error. On a dynamically rendered route this surfaces when the route runs, so it can pass `next build` and fail under `next start`. Read these values outside the cached scope and pass them as arguments. 242 243 ### Runtime caching considerations 244 245 While `use cache` is designed primarily to include uncached data in the static shell, it can also cache data at runtime using in-memory LRU (Least Recently Used) storage. 246 247 With the default in-memory handler, runtime cache behavior depends on your hosting environment: 248 249 | Environment | Runtime Caching Behavior | 250 | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | 251 | **Serverless** | Cache entries typically don't persist across requests (each request can be a different instance), or during revalidation. Build-time caching works normally. | 252 | **Self-hosted** | Cache entries persist across requests. Control cache size with [`cacheMaxMemorySize`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheMaxMemorySize). | 253 254 For example, in a serverless environment, a cached function shared by two pages executes on each static shell revalidation, whereas in self-hosted or environments with persistent memory, the cached output is reused if it's still fresh. 255 256 If the default in-memory cache isn't enough, consider **[`use cache: remote`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote)** which allows platforms to provide a dedicated cache handler (like Redis or KV database). This helps reduce hits against data sources not scaled to your total traffic, though it comes with costs (storage, network latency, platform fees). 257 258 > [!NOTE] 259 > With the default in-memory handler, serverless instances are ephemeral, so entries may not be reused between requests, unlike with `use cache: remote`. Neither caching directive carries over to a new deploy, because the [cache key](#cache-keys) includes the build (or `deploymentId`) ID. 260 > 261 > For data that needs to persist across deploys, use [`unstable_cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/unstable_cache) for non-`fetch` functions or the [`fetch`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch) cache. 262 263 Very rarely, for compliance requirements or when you can't refactor your code to pass runtime data as arguments to a `use cache` scope, you might need [`use cache: private`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private). 264 265 ### Draft Mode 266 267 When [Draft Mode](/docs/app/guides/draft-mode) is enabled, all cached functions and components re-execute on every request, and results are not saved to the cache. This ensures draft content is always fresh without requiring any changes to your caching code. 268 269 You can read `isEnabled` from [`draftMode()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/draft-mode) inside a `use cache` scope, however, other runtime APIs like `cookies()` and `headers()` are not allowed, even when Draft Mode is active. See [Passing runtime values to cached functions](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#passing-runtime-values-to-cached-functions) for the recommended pattern. 270 271 ```tsx filename="app/components/content.tsx" 272 import { draftMode } from 'next/headers' 273 274 async function Content() { 275 'use cache' 276 277 const { isEnabled } = await draftMode() 278 const url = isEnabled 279 ? 'https://draft.example.com/content' 280 : 'https://production.example.com/content' 281 282 const data = await fetch(url) 283 return
{/* ... */}
284 } 285 ``` 286 287 Calling `enable()` or `disable()` inside a caching directive scope will also throw an error. Draft Mode can only be toggled in [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) or [Server Actions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data). 288 289 ### React.cache isolation 290 291 [`React.cache`](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) operates in an isolated scope inside `use cache` boundaries. Values stored via `React.cache` outside a `use cache` function are not visible inside it. 292 293 This means you cannot use `React.cache` to pass data into a `use cache` scope: 294 295 ```tsx 296 import { cache } from 'react' 297 298 const store = cache(() => ({ current: null as string | null })) 299 300 function Parent() { 301 const shared = store() 302 shared.current = 'value from parent' 303 return 304 } 305 306 async function Child() { 307 'use cache' 308 const shared = store() 309 // shared.current is null, not 'value from parent' 310 // use cache has its own isolated React.cache scope 311 return
{shared.current}
312 } 313 ``` 314 315 This isolation ensures cached functions have predictable, self-contained behavior. To pass data into a `use cache` scope, use function arguments instead. 316 317 ## `use cache` at runtime 318 319 On the **server**, cache entries are stored in-memory and respect the `revalidate` and `expire` times from your `cacheLife` configuration. The client router enforces a **minimum 30-second stale time**, regardless of configuration. 322 323 The `x-nextjs-stale-time` response header communicates cache lifetime from server to client, ensuring coordinated behavior. 324 325 ## Revalidation 326 327 Cached functions revalidate based on the `revalidate` and `expire` times in their `cacheLife` profile, or on-demand through tags.
